episodes.155968: A strong cold front spawned a line of showers that produced a sudden onset of gale-force wind over portions of the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay during the overnight hours.
episodes.155969: A strong cold front spawned a line of showers that produced a sudden onset of a couple gale-force wind gusts just prior to midnight local standard time of the middle tidal Potomac River.
episodes.156025: Gusty showers moving across the coast of Brevard County and over the Atlantic waters produced strong winds.
episodes.156026: Strong winds from a severe thunderstorm in rural Okeechobee County resulted in damage at a local farm.
episodes.156763: Thunderstorms developed inland ahead of an approaching cold front and reached the coast in the evening hours. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.156813: A strong outflow boundary with wind gusts near 40 knots raced SSE over the adjacent coastal waters.
episodes.156999: An ice jam developed on the Aroostook River in the vicinity of Fort Fairfield during the 1st causing rising river levels. The rising river levels eventually led to the closure of Riverside Road and Russell Road during the evening of the 1st. The roads remained closed into the evening of the 4th when the ice jam released allowing river levels to fall and allowing the roads to re-open.
episodes.157112: Showers and storms developed along a prefrontal trough that moved through South Florida. As this activity moved offshore into the Atlantic waters, a couple of waterspouts formed over the Atlantic waters.
episodes.157123: Heavy rain on February 28th sent many rivers above flood stage early in March. Minor to moderate flooding occurred on the Ohio, Big Muddy, and Little Wabash Rivers. Persistent above normal rainfall through the month of March kept those rivers above flood stage into the early part of April.
episodes.157125: Minor flooding on the Mississippi River continued from March into the first week of April. An active spring-like pattern in March caused river flooding. There were a couple rounds of heavy rain, somewhere regionally within the Mississippi basin, that contributed to the river flooding.
episodes.157126: Above normal rainfall in late March sent portions of the Ohio and Green Rivers above flood stage in early April. The flooding was minor, consisting of fields and some riverfront parks in the flood plain.
episodes.157568: Heavy rain brought flooding to area rivers at the beginning of April.
